To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the assessment of the more extended, professionally-oriented discourse can be approached in the light of the multilevel assessment approach and that the assessment based enacted curriculum can promote transfer of training across different tasks, situations and levels of understanding.

the assessment of more extensive, professionally oriented discourse should be approached with a view of introducing a way for the development of a type of curricular enactment which fosters transfer, and that the assessment based curriculum enactment approach can be used to promote a curriculum for teaching more extended, professionally-oriented discourse with occupational rather than academic purposes.

a multilevel assessment approach can be used to develop a curriculum for teaching more extended, professionally-oriented discourse, with occupational rather than academic purposes, which fosters transfer across tasks and situations as a deep level understanding in situated lessons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of more complex, extended discourse in the light of a curriculum enactment approach to translator training courses.
the development of an assessment framework for more extended and productive discourse in English for Occupational purposes.

the development of a curriculum for teaching productive domain discourse with occupational purposes which fosters the transfer of foreign language skills across different tasks and settings as well as a deeper level of understanding in a given lesson.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a multilevel assessment approach, which is in line with the enacted curriculum approach in translator training, would help the students to develop a deeper level of understanding of the discourse of their profession, which would lead them to a more productive use of their knowledge of the language in their profession.

the assessment of more complex and extended, professionally oriented, discourse should be approached with a view of promoting an enacted curriculum for teaching more complex, productive domain discourse with occupational rather than academic purposes.
the multilevel assessment approach is a useful and productive tool to be employed in the assessment of the learning process of more complex and extended discourse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multilevel assessment is an approach to the promotion of a productive discourse in translator training courses with professional purposes.
a multilevel assessment practice is a way to promote a type of curriculum that fosters a deep level of learning in the situated lesson.
we have been trying to develop an assessment based curriculum enactment approach to promote productive discourse with professional purposes in the foreign language classroom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assessment of more extensive and complex discourse should not be seen in terms of a one-shot, isolated test or exam.

the multilevel assessment approach can be used in the design of an integrated curriculum which is based on the assessment practice in order to promote the transfer of learning from one situation to another.

a curriculum enactment approach to the teaching of occupational discourse in translator training courses, which is informed by a multilevel assessment practice, is a viable and productive option for the promotion of transfer of learning in foreign language teaching and learning, and, in particular, for the promotion of productive discourse with professional rather academic purposes.
